subject: Re: Redwood integration - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood integration - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya -

Thanks again for taking time this morning to walk through Acme Cloud's recommendation engine needs. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Pain points you called out:
- High latency on real-time reranking for personalization (~350-500ms tail currently)
- Cost pressure from the large batch offline embeddings pipeline
- Lack of structured outputs from the current ML stack makes downstream tooling brittle

Goals you shared:
- Reduce rerank latency to <150ms p95 for in-session UX
- Achieve 5-10x reduction in per-request cost without degrading click-through prediction quality
- Produce consistent structured JSON outputs (intent, entity, score) for downstream services

Technical fit notes (from our discussion):
- Function calling / structured outputs: Redwood's function-calling + structured output mode can map model responses to the JSON schema you already consume. We discussed schema versioning and fallbacks.
- Streaming & partial results: For the reranker, streaming logits/decisions can let the frontend show best-candidate placeholders faster while full rerank finishes.
- Embeddings & reranking: Option to move to a hybrid approach - cached candidate embeddings + on-the-fly lightweight reranker to reduce calls into the full model.
- SDK changes: minimal - our JS/Go SDK supports streaming and function-call bindings out of the box; you may need a small wrapper to convert existing protobufs into the schema we return.

Attachments: attached an integration diagram and an SOW placeholder that outlines the milestones we talked about.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical spike with Vivek (SE) to validate p95 latency on a sample traffic replay (Vivek: can you own scheduling?)
2) SOW draft + pricing estimate (attached) - Marissa to follow up with a formal proposal by EOD Friday
3) Data access: Acme to share a sanitized sample of 10k request/response pairs for replay testing
4) If spike looks good, schedule a 2-week integration pilot with Dedicated capacity reserved

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

--

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecloud.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa - great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- For latency: the 350-500ms number is for our current online stack including network overhead. The product team wants end-to-end p95 under 200ms; if Redwood can hit <150ms server-side, we're in good shape.
- For structured outputs: we liked the idea of function-calling but need guarantees for schema stability across model updates. Can you include a versioning/fallback approach in the SOW?
- On the data sample: we'll sanitize and share 10k rows by Monday. Priya will coordinate.

Vivek - can we do the replay with ~100 RPS sustained to simulate peak? If not, let us know what config you need.

Marissa - thanks for taking the lead on the SOW and pricing. Also curious if you have a sense of typical cost delta between Dedicated reserved pools vs hosted API for a workload like ours.

Best,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager | Acme Cloud
jordan.miles@acmecloud.com

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration - post-call recap & next steps

Jordan - thanks, noted on the p95 target and schema stability. Quick follow-up to address the two asks and to loop Dev in on the SDK/technical integration side.

1) Replay config: Vivek, our standard replay harness can simulate 100-200 RPS depending on instance sizing. For a realistic p95 test at 100 RPS we'll provision a small Dedicated pool with a single reserved node and run a traffic replay for the spike. I'll coordinate available windows next week.

2) Schema versioning: we propose the following in the SOW (high level):
   - Responses include a schema_version field; major upgrades require a 30-day deprecation notice and we include a compatibility mode that returns a best-effort older-shape payload when compatibility flag is set.
   - Function-calling bindings will be explicit in the SDK so you can map to your protobufs.

3) SDK changes: Dev - can you review the two minimal changes we discussed: (a) add a small adapter to translate Acme's current result protobuf to Redwood's function-call expected input, (b) a streaming consumer to accept partial reranker outputs and merge with your frontend placeholder flow. Estimated effort: ~2-3 dev days.

Jordan/Priya - if you can share the sanitized dataset and an initial list of schema fields we can draft a compatibility test plan.

Marissa

--

Internal only - prepping the SE/dev checklist for the Acme replay spike and pilot. Please treat as internal.

Summary of asked deliverables:
- Schedule: aim to run the 100 RPS replay next Wed (May 5) morning PST - Vivek to confirm exact time and infra needs.
- Data: Acme will deliver sanitized 10k request/response pairs by Monday EOD (Priya). We'll validate size/format on Tuesday.
- SOW: I'll finalize draft SOW with pricing bands for Hosted vs Dedicated by EOD Friday (May 1). Include schema versioning and a 30-day deprecation clause.
- Dev work: Dev to create adapter + streaming consumer pattern; estimate 2-3 days of effort and a short runbook for the frontend team.
- Success criteria for pilot: p95 < 150ms server-side, no >3% drop in rerank quality (measured by CTR proxy), and structured outputs correctly mapped in >99% of test cases.

Vivek / Dev - please reply here with any blockers or additional infra reqs. I'll keep Jordan and Priya in the loop once we have confirmed windows and SOW.
